title: "10 — Species context classification"
format: html
execute: {echo: false, warning: false, message: false}

## Question

Which eligible species are consistently positive, consistently negative, or cross zero across their own observed climate support?

## Dataset and sample size

Eligible units are drawn from 526 modeled species; exact eligible counts and class counts are shown below.

## Exact model specification

Conditional coefficients come from anchored `M_both`. Extrema are evaluated within each species' observed destination T-P hull at the anchored median warming context.

## Assumptions

Eligibility requires at least four experiments and a full-rank within-species
climate design. Classification is evaluated only inside each eligible species'
observed climate support.

## Convergence and covariance diagnostics

This step fits no model; it inherits the Step 09 convergence and covariance gates.

## Main numerical results

```{r}
summary <- targets::tar_read(species_classification_summary)
classification <- targets::tar_read(species_classification_526)
examples <- targets::tar_read(species_callout_examples_526)
knitr::kable(summary)
knitr::kable(examples[, c("species_id", "fitted_class", "selection_rank_within_class", "selection_rule")])
knitr::kable(head(classification[order(classification$fitted_class, classification$species_id), ], 20))
```

## PASS/FAIL

Eligibility requires at least four experiments and a full-rank within-species climate design.
The four callout species are selected by the documented within-class rules and are not chosen during rendering.

## Interpretation boundary

Classes summarize fitted response over observed support; they are not significance-based upstream winner/loser labels.

## Canonical objects

`species_context_bundle_526`, `species_classification_526`, and `species_callout_examples_526`.
